- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and price is falling, model frequently undercorrects; add 1–2% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in early forecast periods (e.g., first 5–7 days); adjust downward if recent history shows persistent upward momentum.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.8) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, apply “lag correction”: reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period, especially if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, model often overestimates downward trends; apply downward bias of 2–4% if sentiment is negative or sentiment is trending downward.
